name: Rf_getAttrib
summary: Get or set the attribute associated with a symbol.
signature:
SEXP Rf_getAttrib(SEXP x, SEXP symbol);
SEXP Rf_setAttrib(SEXP x, SEXP symbol, SEXP value);
returns: `Rf_getAttrib()` returns the value of the attribute, or `R_NilValue` if `x` has no such attribute; `Rf_setAttrib()` returns `value`.
notes:
`Rf_getAttrib()` normally returns a borrowed reference, but there is one
exception: retrieving `row.names` from a data frame expands the compact
`c(NA_integer_, -n)` form into a newly allocated vector, which must be
protected.

name: Rf_copyMostAttrib
summary: Copy attributes, except names, dim, and dimnames, from one object to another.

name: DUPLICATE_ATTRIB
summary: Copy attributes from one object to another when duplicating an object.
signature:
void DUPLICATE_ATTRIB(SEXP to, SEXP from);
void SHALLOW_DUPLICATE_ATTRIB(SEXP to, SEXP from);

name: Rf_isArray
summary: Test if an object is an array.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` is an array (a vector with a `dim` attribute), otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Arrays are vectors with a dim attribute.

name: Rf_allocArray
summary: Create an array of the given type and dimensions.
signature:
SEXP Rf_allocArray(SEXPTYPE type, SEXP dims);
SEXP Rf_alloc3DArray(SEXPTYPE type, int, int, int);
returns: A newly allocated array of the given type and dimensions.

name: Rf_GetArrayDimnames
summary: Get the dimnames of an array.
returns: The dimnames of `x` as a list, or `R_NilValue` if it has none.

name: Rf_dimgets
summary: Set the dim or dimnames attribute of an array.
signature:
SEXP Rf_dimgets(SEXP x, SEXP v);
SEXP Rf_dimnamesgets(SEXP x, SEXP v);
returns: The modified object `x`.

args.v: the new dim (an integer vector) or dimnames (a list).

name: Rf_DropDims
summary: Drop the dim attribute of an array.
returns: `x` with its `dim` attribute removed.

name: Rf_arraySubscript
summary: Compute the vector offset corresponding to an array subscript.
signature: SEXP Rf_arraySubscript(int, SEXP, SEXP, SEXP (*)(SEXP,SEXP), SEXP (*)(SEXP, int), SEXP);
returns: A newly allocated vector of offsets into the array's underlying storage.

name: Rf_allocMatrix
summary: Create a matrix of the given type and dimensions.
signature: SEXP Rf_allocMatrix(SEXPTYPE type, int nrow, int ncol);
returns: A newly allocated matrix of the given type and dimensions.
notes: Matrices are arrays with exactly 2 dimensions.

name: Rf_isMatrix
summary: Test if an object is a matrix.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` is a matrix (an array with exactly two dimensions), otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_GetColNames
summary: Get the column or row names from a dimnames object.
signature:
SEXP Rf_GetColNames(SEXP dimnames);
SEXP Rf_GetRowNames(SEXP dimnames);
returns: `Rf_GetColNames()` returns the column names (second element of `dimnames`) and `Rf_GetRowNames()` the row names (first element); either may be `R_NilValue`.

name: Rf_GetMatrixDimnames
summary: Get the row and column names of a matrix through output parameters.
signature:
void Rf_GetMatrixDimnames(SEXP x, SEXP* rl, SEXP* cl,
  const char** rownames, const char** colnames);

args.rl: output parameter for the row names as a SEXP.
args.cl: output parameter for the column names as a SEXP.
args.rownames: output parameter for the row names as C strings.
args.colnames: output parameter for the column names as C strings.

name: Rf_ncols
summary: Get the number of columns or rows of a matrix.
signature:
int Rf_ncols(SEXP x);
int Rf_nrows(SEXP x);
returns: The number of columns (`Rf_ncols()`) or rows (`Rf_nrows()`) of `x`.

name: Rf_copyMatrix
summary: Copy the contents of one matrix into another.
signature:
void Rf_copyMatrix(SEXP source, SEXP target, Rboolean byrow);
void Rf_copyListMatrix(SEXP source, SEXP target, Rboolean byrow);

name: Rf_isFactor
summary: Test if an object is a factor, or an ordered or unordered factor.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` is a factor (`Rf_isFactor()`), an ordered factor (`Rf_isOrdered()`), or an unordered factor (`Rf_isUnordered()`), otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_nlevels
summary: Get the number of levels of a factor.
returns: The number of levels of the factor `x`.

name: Rf_asCharacterFactor
summary: Coerce a factor into a character vector.
returns: A newly allocated character vector of the factor's level labels.

name: Rf_namesgets
summary: Set the names of a vector.
returns: The input vector with its names set.

name: Rf_conformable
summary: Test whether two objects have conformable dimensions.
returns: `TRUE` if the two objects have conformable dimensions, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_isTs
summary: Test whether an object is a time series.
returns: `TRUE` if the object is of class `ts`, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
Tests for the `"ts"` class. Mostly of historical interest: the `ts`
class (a numeric vector or matrix with a `tsp` attribute) is base R's
original time series representation, but most modern time series
packages use their own classes.

name: Rf_isDataFrame
summary: Test whether an object is a data frame.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` is a data frame, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: R_getAttributes
summary: Query the attributes of an object as a whole.
returns: `R_getAttributes()` returns the attributes of `x` as a named list (`R_NilValue` if none); `R_getAttribCount()` returns the number of attributes; `R_getAttribNames()` returns their names as a character vector; `R_hasAttrib()` returns `true` if `x` has an attribute called `name`.
notes:
`R_getAttributes()` returns the attributes as a named list, like
`attributes()`; `R_hasAttrib()` tests for one attribute by name
without retrieving it.

name: R_nrow
summary: Get the number of rows or columns of a matrix or data frame.
signature:
R_xlen_t R_nrow(SEXP x);
R_xlen_t R_ncol(SEXP x);
returns: The number of rows (`R_nrow()`) or columns (`R_ncol()`) of `x`.
notes:
May dispatch to the `dim` method for non-standard objects, so they
can allocate and error.

name: R_class
summary: Get the class vector of an object.
returns: The class vector of `x`, or the implicit class if `x` has no class attribute.
notes:
Returns the implicit class for classless objects, like `class()`
does; use `Rf_getAttrib(x, R_ClassSymbol)` if you want only the
explicit class attribute.

name: R_mapAttrib
summary: Iterate over the attributes of an object with a callback.
signature: SEXP R_mapAttrib(SEXP x, SEXP (*FUN)(SEXP, SEXP, void *), void *data);
returns: The first non-`NULL` value returned by `FUN`, or `NULL` if `FUN` returned `NULL` for every attribute.

args.FUN: called with each attribute's name and value; return `NULL` to continue, or any other value to stop and return it.

notes:
Highly experimental: both interface and semantics may change at short
notice. Use only when `Rf_getAttrib()`/`R_getAttributes()` can't do
the job.

name: ANY_ATTRIB
summary: Test for, or remove, all attributes.
returns: `ANY_ATTRIB()` returns non-zero if `x` has any attributes, otherwise zero.
notes:
`CLEAR_ATTRIB()` removes all attributes and clears the object and
S4 bits. Prefer `Rf_getAttrib()`/`Rf_setAttrib()` when you only
touch one attribute.

name: R_registerRoutines
summary: Register a package's native routines and restrict dynamic symbol lookup.
returns: `R_registerRoutines()` returns the number of routines registered; `R_useDynamicSymbols()` returns the previous setting.

args.callRoutines: NULL-terminated array of `R_CallMethodDef` entries: name, function pointer cast to `DL_FUNC`, argument count.
args.value: `FALSE` hides unregistered symbols, so routines can only be reached via registration.

notes:
Call from `R_init_<pkgname>()`. Generate the registration boilerplate
with `tools::package_native_routine_registration_skeleton("src")`.

name: R_RegisterCCallable
summary: Export or retrieve a C entry point for use by another package.
signature:
void R_RegisterCCallable(const char *package, const char *name, DL_FUNC fptr);
DL_FUNC R_GetCCallable(const char *package, const char *name);
returns: `R_GetCCallable()` returns the registered function pointer, raising an error if not found.
notes:
Register in `R_init_<package>()`; clients retrieve the pointer at
their own load time and call it directly, with no R-level dispatch.
The function pointer must remain valid while the providing package
is loaded.

name: R_FindSymbol
summary: Look up a symbol in a loaded DLL by name.
signature: DL_FUNC R_FindSymbol(char const *name, char const *pkg, DllInfo *info);
returns: The entry point for `name`, or `NULL` if not found.
notes:
Searches the DLLs loaded for package `pkg` (`info` is filled in if
not `NULL`). Rarely needed now that `R_GetCCallable()` exists.

name: R_forceSymbols
summary: Restrict a DLL to registered (symbol) entry points.
returns: The previous setting.
notes:
With `value = TRUE`, entry points of the DLL can only be called via
registered `R_CallMethodDef` symbols, not by name. Set in
`R_init_<package>()` alongside `R_useDynamicSymbols(dll, FALSE)`.

name: R_cycle_detected
summary: Detect a reference cycle between two objects.
returns: `TRUE` if there is a reference cycle between the two objects, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: IS_GETTER_CALL
summary: Test whether a call is a getter call in complex assignment support.
notes:
Used internally to distinguish getter from setter calls in complex
assignment support.

name: ATTRIB
summary: Get or set the pairlist containing an object's attributes.
signature:
SEXP ATTRIB(SEXP x);
void SET_ATTRIB(SEXP x, SEXP v);
returns: `ATTRIB()` returns the attribute pairlist of `x`, or `R_NilValue` if it has none.
notes:
Not part of the API, since it exposes the internal linked-list
representation of attributes. Use `Rf_getAttrib()`/`Rf_setAttrib()` for
individual attributes, `DUPLICATE_ATTRIB()`/`SHALLOW_DUPLICATE_ATTRIB()`
to copy attributes between objects, `CLEAR_ATTRIB()` (R 4.5.0) to remove
all attributes, `ANY_ATTRIB()` (R 4.5.0) to test for any attributes, and
`R_mapAttrib()` (R 4.6.0) to iterate over attributes.

name: Rf_isFrame
summary: Test if an object is a data frame.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` is a data frame, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Prefer `Rf_isDataFrame()` (added in R 4.5.0) in new code.

name: R_NamespaceRegistry
summary: Access the registry of registered namespaces.
notes:
Not part of the API; use `R_getRegisteredNamespace()` to find a
registered namespace.

name: Rf_findVar
summary: Find the value bound to a symbol in an environment and its enclosing environments.
returns: The value bound to `symbol` in `environment` or its enclosing environments.
notes:
May allocate, since the binding it finds could be an active binding.
Too low level to be part of the API; prefer `R_getVar()` or
`R_getVarEx()` (added in R 4.5.0) in new code.

name: Rf_findVarInFrame3
summary: Find a symbol in a single environment, without searching enclosing environments.
signature:
SEXP Rf_findVarInFrame3(SEXP env, SEXP symbol, Rboolean doGet);
SEXP Rf_findVarInFrame(SEXP env, SEXP symbol);
returns: The value bound to `symbol` in `env`, or `R_UnboundValue` if not found.

args.doGet: if `TRUE`, returns the value; if `FALSE`, just checks for presence.

notes:
Returns `R_UnboundValue` if not found. `Rf_findVarInFrame()` is shorthand
for `Rf_findVarInFrame3(rho, symbol, TRUE)`. Too low level to be part of
the API; prefer `R_getVar()` or `R_getVarEx()` (added in R 4.5.0) to
retrieve a value and `R_existsVarInFrame()` to test for existence.

name: Rf_addMissingVarsToNewEnv
summary: Copy variables into a new environment unless already present.
notes: Copies variables from `from` (a `VECSXP`) unless already present in `to`.

name: R_envHasNoSpecialSymbols
summary: Test whether an environment has no special symbols.
returns: `TRUE` if the environment contains no special symbols, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: FRAME
summary: Get or set the frame of an environment.
signature:
SEXP FRAME(SEXP x);
void SET_FRAME(SEXP x, SEXP v);
returns: `FRAME()` returns the frame (binding pairlist) of environment `x`.
notes:
`SET_FRAME()` is not part of the API; create environments with the
constructor `R_NewEnv()` instead of mutating an environment's frame.

name: ENCLOS
summary: Get or set an environment's enclosing environment.
signature:
SEXP ENCLOS(SEXP x);
void SET_ENCLOS(SEXP x, SEXP v);
returns: `ENCLOS()` returns the enclosing environment of `x`.
notes:
Use `R_ParentEnv()` (added in R 4.5.0) instead of `ENCLOS()`. To choose
the enclosing environment of a new environment, use the constructor
`R_NewEnv()` rather than `SET_ENCLOS()`.

name: ENVFLAGS
summary: Get or set the flags of an environment.
signature:
int ENVFLAGS(SEXP x);
void SET_ENVFLAGS(SEXP x, int v);
returns: `ENVFLAGS()` returns the flags of environment `x`.
notes: Use `R_EnvironmentIsLocked()` and `R_LockEnvironment()` instead.

name: TRUELENGTH
summary: Get or set the truelength of an object.
returns: `TRUELENGTH()` returns the truelength of `x` as an `int`; `XTRUELENGTH()` returns it as an `R_xlen_t`.
notes:
Rarely used, mainly for hash tables of environments (`VECSXP`s), where
length is the table size and truelength is the number of primary slots
in use, and for the reference hash tables used in serialization, where
truelength is the number of slots in use.

name: HASHTAB
summary: Get or set the hash table of an environment.
signature:
SEXP HASHTAB(SEXP x);
void SET_HASHTAB(SEXP x, SEXP v);
returns: `HASHTAB()` returns the hash table of environment `x`, or `R_NilValue` if it is not hashed.
notes:
Hashing speeds up searching environments that are added to often but
rarely deleted from; removed bindings are not actually deleted but have
their value set to `R_UnboundValue`. `SET_HASHTAB()` is not part of the
API; create hash-based environments with the constructor `R_NewEnv()`
instead.

name: HASHASH
summary: Get or set the hash flag of an environment.
signature:
int HASHASH(SEXP x);
void SET_HASHASH(SEXP x, int v);
returns: `HASHASH()` returns nonzero if environment `x` uses a hash table, otherwise zero.

name: HASHVALUE
summary: Get or set the hash value of an environment.
signature:
int HASHVALUE(SEXP x);
void SET_HASHVALUE(SEXP x, int v);
returns: `HASHVALUE()` returns the hash value stored in `x`.

name: EXTPTR_PTR
summary: Access the fields of an external pointer directly.
signature:
#define EXTPTR_PTR(x)	CAR(x)
#define EXTPTR_PROT(x)	CDR(x)
#define EXTPTR_TAG(x)	TAG(x)
notes:
Read the fields directly from the underlying cons cell. Use
`R_ExternalPtrAddr()`, `R_ExternalPtrProtected()`, and
`R_ExternalPtrTag()` instead.

name: FORMALS
summary: Access the formal arguments, body, or environment of a closure.
returns: `FORMALS()` returns the formal argument list of closure `x`; `BODY()` returns its body; `CLOENV()` returns its environment.
notes:
Superseded by `R_ClosureFormals()`, `R_ClosureBody()`, and
`R_ClosureEnv()` (R 4.5.0).

name: SET_FORMALS
summary: Set the formal arguments, body, or environment of a closure.
notes:
Superseded by the constructor `R_mkClosure()` (R 4.5.0); prefer building
a closure over allocating and mutating one.

name: RDEBUG
summary: Query the debug, step, or trace flags of a closure.
returns: `RDEBUG()`, `RSTEP()`, and `RTRACE()` return the debug, step, and trace flags of closure `x`, respectively.
notes: Internal macros for querying closure debugging flags.

name: SET_RDEBUG
summary: Set the debug, step, or trace flags of a closure.
notes: Internal macros for setting closure debugging flags.

name: PRCODE
summary: Access the code, environment, or value of a promise.
returns: `PRCODE()` returns the promise's code; `PRENV()` returns its environment; `PRVALUE()` returns its value, or `R_UnboundValue` if not yet forced.
notes:
Superseded by the R 4.6.0 binding-access API: `R_GetBindingType()`,
`R_ForcedBindingExpression()`, `R_DelayedBindingExpression()`, and
`R_DelayedBindingEnvironment()`.

name: PRSEEN
summary: Query or set the seen flag of a promise.
returns: `PRSEEN()` returns the seen flag of promise `x`.
notes: Used to detect recursive promise evaluation.

name: SET_PRENV
summary: Set the environment, value, or code of a promise.
notes:
Superseded by the R 4.6.0 binding-access API: `R_MakeForcedBinding()`,
`R_MakeDelayedBinding()`, and `R_MakeMissingBinding()`.

name: IS_S4_OBJECT
summary: Test, set, or clear the S4 object flag on a SEXP.
returns: `IS_S4_OBJECT()` returns nonzero if `x` is an S4 object, otherwise zero.
notes: Low-level access to the S4 object flag.

name: CONS_NR
summary: Create a CONS cell with no reference counting.
returns: A newly allocated cons cell with car `a` and cdr `b`.
notes: CONS with no-refcounting?

name: R_InitConnOutPStream
summary: Initialise a persistence stream that reads from or writes to a connection.
notes:
The connection interface is not available to packages. Define
`NEED_CONNECTION_PSTREAMS` before including `Rinternals.h` to get the
opaque `Rconnection` pointer type.

name: R_RestoreHashCount
summary: Restore the hash count of a hashed environment after unserialisation.

name: SET_PRINTNAME
summary: Set the print name of a symbol.
notes:
Symbols are interned and shared; mutating a print name corrupts the
symbol table. Create the symbol you want with `Rf_install()` instead.

name: SYMVALUE
summary: Get or set the value of a symbol.
signature:
SEXP (SYMVALUE)(SEXP x);
void SET_SYMVALUE(SEXP x, SEXP v);
returns: `SYMVALUE()` returns the value bound to symbol `x`.

name: INTERNAL
summary: Get or set the internal function a symbol points to.
signature:
SEXP (INTERNAL)(SEXP x);
void SET_INTERNAL(SEXP x, SEXP v);
returns: `INTERNAL()` returns the internal function that symbol `x` points to.

name: DDVAL
summary: Get or set a symbol's `...` index, or install the symbol for a `...` element.
returns: `DDVAL()` returns the `...` index of symbol `x`; `Rf_installDDVAL()` returns the symbol for the `i`-th `...` element.

name: BCODE_CODE
summary: Access the components of a byte-code object.
signature:
#define BCODE_CODE(x)   CAR(x)
#define BCODE_CONSTS(x) CDR(x)
#define BCODE_EXPR(x)   TAG(x)
#define isByteCode(x)   (TYPEOF(x)==BCODESXP)

name: R_initialize_bcode
summary: Initialize the byte-code engine.

name: R_bcEncode
summary: Encode or decode a byte-code object.
returns: `R_bcEncode()` returns the byte-code encoding of its argument; `R_bcDecode()` returns the decoded object.

name: R_PromiseExpr
summary: Get the unevaluated expression of a promise.
returns: The unevaluated expression of the promise.
notes:
`R_PromiseExpr()` is not part of the API; use the binding access API
added in R 4.6.0 (e.g. `R_DelayedBindingExpression()`) to inspect
promise bindings.

name: Rf_allocSExp
summary: Allocate a non-vector SEXP of the given type.
returns: A newly allocated non-vector `SEXP` of the given type.
notes:
Not part of the API, as it exposes internal structure that might need to
change. Use an appropriate constructor instead: `R_NewEnv()` for
environments, `R_mkClosure()` for closures (added in R 4.5.0), or
`Rf_allocLang()` for call expressions (added in R 4.4.1).

name: Rf_applyClosure
summary: Apply a closure to a list of arguments.
signature: SEXP Rf_applyClosure(SEXP, SEXP, SEXP, SEXP, SEXP);
returns: The result of applying the closure to the arguments.

name: Rf_countContexts
summary: Count evaluation contexts on the context stack.
returns: The number of matching contexts on the context stack.

name: Rf_CreateTag
summary: Create the tag for a pairlist element.
returns: The newly created tag for a pairlist element.

name: Rf_installS3Signature
summary: Install the signature string for an S3 method.
returns: The installed symbol for the S3 signature string.

name: Rf_isFree
summary: Test whether a symbol has no value binding.
returns: `TRUE` if the symbol has no value binding, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_readS3VarsFromFrame
summary: Read the S3 dispatch variables from a method's evaluation frame.
signature: void Rf_readS3VarsFromFrame(SEXP, SEXP*, SEXP*, SEXP*, SEXP*, SEXP*, SEXP*);

name: Rf_setSVector
summary: Set an element of a C array of SEXPs.

name: R_dot_Last
summary: Run shutdown actions when R exits.
notes:
Shutdown actions: `R_dot_Last()` runs the `.Last()` function (in
main.c); `R_RunExitFinalizers()` runs finalizers registered for exit
(in memory.c).

name: R_FixupRHS
summary: Fix up the right-hand side value of a complex assignment.
returns: The fixed-up right-hand side value of the complex assignment.

name: setIVector
summary: Fill an int or double array with a constant value.

name: SETLENGTH
summary: Set the length of a vector in place.
notes:
Uppercase, macro variant of `Rf_lengthgets()`. For resizable (growable)
vectors, see `R_allocResizableVector()` and `R_resizeVector()` (R 4.6.0).
`SETLENGTH()` errors if applied to an ALTREP vector.

name: STRING_PTR
summary: Get a pointer to the elements of a character vector.
returns: A writable pointer to the `SEXP` elements of character vector `x`.
notes:
A writable pointer to character vector data can violate the memory
manager's integrity assumptions and is not supported; use
`STRING_PTR_RO()` instead.

name: VECTOR_PTR
summary: Get a pointer to the elements of a list.
returns: A pointer to the `SEXP` elements of list `x`; currently always throws an error instead.
notes: A deprecated interface that now throws an error.

name: Rf_GetOption
summary: Retrieve the value of an R option (two-argument form).
returns: The value of the option, or `R_NilValue` if it is not set.
notes: Removed from the headers in R 4.6.0; use `Rf_GetOption1()`.

name: R_popen
summary: Open a pipe or run a command in a shell.
signature:
FILE *R_popen(const char *, const char *);
int R_system(const char *);
returns: `R_popen()` returns a `FILE` pointer to the pipe, or `NULL` on failure; `R_system()` returns the command's exit status.
notes:
Removed from the headers in R 4.6.0. There is no C-level API
replacement; use `system()` or a pipe connection at the R level.

name: R_FlushConsole
summary: Flush the console.
notes: Only meaningful for front-ends; WRE classifies it as embedding-only.

name: R_RunPendingFinalizers
summary: Run any pending finalizers.
notes:
Only meaningful for front-ends driving the event loop; WRE
classifies it as embedding-only.

name: R_GlobalEnv
summary: Access the global environment.
notes: The "global" environment.

name: R_EmptyEnv
summary: Access the empty environment.
notes: An empty environment at the root of the environment tree.

name: R_BaseEnv
summary: Access the base environment.
notes: The base environment; formerly `R_NilValue`.

name: R_BaseNamespace
summary: Access the base namespace.
notes: The (fake) namespace for base.

name: R_NewEnv
summary: Create a new environment.
signature: SEXP R_NewEnv(SEXP enclos, int hash, int size);
returns: The newly allocated environment, with enclosure `enclos`.

name: Rf_findFun
summary: Find the function bound to a symbol in an environment and its enclosing environments.
returns: The function bound to `symbol` in `environment` or an enclosing frame.
notes: Like `Rf_findVar()`, but ignores non-functions.

name: Rf_defineVar
summary: Bind a symbol to a value in an environment.
signature: void Rf_defineVar(SEXP symbol, SEXP value, SEXP env);
notes: To remove a binding, set its value to `R_UnboundSymbol`.

name: R_lsInternal3
summary: List the names bound in an environment.
signature: SEXP R_lsInternal3(SEXP env, Rboolean all_names, Rboolean sorted);
returns: A freshly allocated character vector of the names bound in `env`.
notes:
Returns a character vector. The older `R_lsInternal(env, all)` was
removed from the headers in R 4.6.0.

name: Rf_isEnvironment
summary: Test whether an object is an environment.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` is an environment (`ENVSXP`), otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Equivalent to `TYPEOF(x) == ENVSXP`.

name: R_IsPackageEnv
summary: Test whether an environment is a package environment, get its name, or find a package's environment.
returns: `R_IsPackageEnv()` returns `TRUE` if `rho` is a package environment, otherwise `FALSE`; `R_PackageEnvName()` returns its name as a string, or `R_NilValue` if not a package environment; `R_FindPackageEnv()` returns the environment of the named package.

name: R_IsNamespaceEnv
summary: Test whether an environment is a namespace environment, get its spec, or find a namespace.
returns: `R_IsNamespaceEnv()` returns `TRUE` if `rho` is a namespace, otherwise `FALSE`; `R_NamespaceEnvSpec()` returns its spec string, or `R_NilValue` if not a namespace; `R_FindNamespace()` returns the named namespace environment.

name: R_LockEnvironment
summary: Lock an environment, or test whether it is locked.
signature:
void R_LockEnvironment(SEXP env, Rboolean bindings);
Rboolean R_EnvironmentIsLocked(SEXP env);
returns: `R_EnvironmentIsLocked()` returns `TRUE` if `env` is locked, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: R_LockBinding
summary: Lock or unlock a binding in an environment.
signature:
void R_LockBinding(SEXP sym, SEXP env);
void R_unLockBinding(SEXP sym, SEXP env);

name: R_MakeActiveBinding
summary: Make an active binding for a symbol in an environment.
signature: void R_MakeActiveBinding(SEXP sym, SEXP fun, SEXP env);

name: R_BindingIsLocked
summary: Test whether a binding is locked or active.
signature:
Rboolean R_BindingIsLocked(SEXP sym, SEXP env);
Rboolean R_BindingIsActive(SEXP sym, SEXP env);
returns: `TRUE` if the binding of `sym` in `env` is locked (`R_BindingIsLocked()`) or active (`R_BindingIsActive()`), otherwise `FALSE`.

name: R_HasFancyBindings
summary: Test whether an environment has fancy bindings.
returns: `TRUE` if `rho` has any active or delayed bindings, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_setVar
summary: Assign a value to a symbol in an environment.
signature:
void Rf_setVar(SEXP, SEXP, SEXP);
void Rf_gsetVar(SEXP, SEXP, SEXP);

name: R_getVar
summary: Get the value of a variable from an environment.
signature:
SEXP R_getVar(SEXP sym, SEXP env, Rboolean inherits);
SEXP R_getVarEx(SEXP sym, SEXP env, Rboolean inherits, SEXP ifnotfound);
returns: The value of `sym` in `env`, searching enclosing frames if `inherits` is `TRUE` (not freshly allocated); `R_getVarEx()` returns `ifnotfound` when not found, while `R_getVar()` errors.

args.inherits: search enclosing frames, as `inherits = TRUE` in `get()`.
args.ifnotfound: `R_getVarEx` only: value returned when the variable is not found, as in `get0()`.

notes:
The API replacement for the non-API `Rf_findVar()`/
`Rf_findVarInFrame()`. `R_getVar()` errors when the variable is not
found. Active bindings are triggered and delayed bindings are forced.

name: R_ParentEnv
summary: Get the enclosing environment of an environment.
returns: The enclosing (parent) environment of `env`; errors on the empty environment.
notes: The API replacement for `ENCLOS()`; errors on the empty environment.

name: R_GetBindingType
summary: Query the type of a symbol's binding in an environment.
returns: The binding type of `sym` in `env`: one of `R_BindingTypeUnbound`, `R_BindingTypeValue`, `R_BindingTypeMissing`, `R_BindingTypeDelayed`, `R_BindingTypeForced`, or `R_BindingTypeActive`.
notes:
Returns one of `R_BindingTypeUnbound`, `R_BindingTypeValue`,
`R_BindingTypeMissing`, `R_BindingTypeDelayed`,
`R_BindingTypeForced`, or `R_BindingTypeActive`. Part of the
experimental binding API added in R 4.6.0; the interface may change.

name: R_DelayedBindingExpression
summary: Inspect the expression or environment behind a delayed or forced binding.
returns: `R_DelayedBindingExpression()` returns the delayed expression, `R_DelayedBindingEnvironment()` the environment it will be evaluated in, and `R_ForcedBindingExpression()` the expression behind a forced binding.
notes: Use `R_GetBindingType()` first to check the binding type.

name: R_MakeDelayedBinding
summary: Create a delayed, forced, or missing binding in an environment.

args.expr: the expression associated with the binding.
args.evalEnv: environment in which a delayed binding's expression is evaluated.

notes:
A delayed binding is a promise; a forced binding pairs an expression
with its already-computed value; a missing binding is one whose
argument was not supplied.

name: R_envSymbols
summary: List the symbols bound in an environment.
returns: A freshly allocated list of the symbols bound in `env`.

name: R_findDotsEnv
summary: Find the nearest enclosing frame containing a `...` binding.
signature:
SEXP R_findDotsEnv(SEXP env);
Rboolean R_DotsExist(SEXP env);
returns: `R_findDotsEnv()` returns the nearest enclosing frame containing a `...` binding, or `R_EmptyEnv` if none; `R_DotsExist()` returns `TRUE` if `env` contains a `...` binding, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
`R_findDotsEnv()` walks parent environments and returns the first
containing a proper `...` binding, or `R_EmptyEnv`. The `R_Dots*`/`R_Dot*`
accessors look up `...` only in the given frame, so call this first if
you need R's inherited lookup.

name: R_DotsLength
summary: Get the length or names of the `...` binding in a frame.
signature:
int R_DotsLength(SEXP env);
SEXP R_DotsNames(SEXP env);
returns: `R_DotsLength()` returns the number of elements in the `...` binding of `env`; `R_DotsNames()` returns their names as a character vector.

name: R_GetDotType
summary: Query the type of an individual `...` element.
returns: The type of `...` element `i`: one of `R_DotTypeValue`, `R_DotTypeMissing`, `R_DotTypeDelayed`, or `R_DotTypeForced`.
notes:
Returns one of `R_DotTypeValue`, `R_DotTypeMissing`,
`R_DotTypeDelayed`, or `R_DotTypeForced`.

name: R_DotsElt
summary: Access an individual `...` element or its underlying expression.
returns: `R_DotsElt()` returns the (forced) value of `...` element `i`; the `R_Dot*` variants return the underlying expression or evaluation environment without forcing it.
notes:
`R_DotsElt()` forces the element, like `...elt()`; the `R_Dot*`
variants inspect a delayed or forced element without forcing — check
with `R_GetDotType()` first.

name: Rf_topenv
summary: Find the top-level environment in an environment chain.
returns: The top-level environment in the chain containing `x`, stopping at `target`.

args.target: stop when this environment is reached, usually `R_NilValue`.

name: R_GetCurrentEnv
summary: Retrieve the environment of the currently executing closure.
returns: The environment of the closure currently being evaluated; only meaningful while R is evaluating a call.
notes:
Only meaningful while R is evaluating a call. Usually better to pass
the environment explicitly as an argument to your C function.

name: Rf_error
summary: Signal an error, optionally including the call in the message.
signature:
void Rf_error(const char* format, ...);
void Rf_errorcall(SEXP call, const char* format, ...);
notes: Use `Rf_errorcall(R_NilValue, ...)` to suppress display of the call.

name: Rf_warning
summary: Signal a warning, optionally including the call or displaying it immediately.

name: error_return
summary: Eliminate compiler warnings about non-void functions that don't return.
signature:
#define error_return(msg) { \
  Rf_error(msg); \
  return R_NilValue; \
}
#define errorcall_return(cl,msg) { \
  Rf_errorcall(cl, msg); \
  return R_NilValue; \
}
notes:
`Rf_error` will `longjmp` and so any code following will not be executed;
however, most compilers do not detect this when providing warnings.

name: R_UnwindProtect
summary: Run a C function, guaranteeing a cleanup action runs on normal return and on longjmp.
returns: The `SEXP` returned by `fun`.

args.fun: function to run; its return value is passed through.
args.clean: cleanup function, called with `jump = FALSE` after a normal return and `jump = TRUE` before a non-local transfer of control resumes.
args.cont: continuation token from `R_MakeUnwindCont()`, or `R_NilValue` for plain C use.

notes:
This is the primary tool for making C (and C++) code longjmp-safe: free
`R_Calloc()` memory, close files, and restore state in `clean`. With a
continuation token, `clean` can throw a C++ exception to unwind the C++
stack and then call `R_ContinueUnwind()` to resume R's longjmp.

name: R_MakeUnwindCont
summary: Allocate a continuation token for C++ stack unwinding, and resume the unwind.
signature:
SEXP R_MakeUnwindCont(void);
NORET void R_ContinueUnwind(SEXP cont);
returns: `R_MakeUnwindCont()` returns a `SEXP` continuation token for use with `R_UnwindProtect()`; `R_ContinueUnwind()` never returns.
notes:
`PROTECT` the token before passing it to `R_UnwindProtect()`. Only needed
when C++ code sits between R and the cleanup handler; plain C code should
pass `R_NilValue` as `cont` instead.

name: R_ExecWithCleanup
summary: Execute a C function in a protected context, with cleanup before teardown.
returns: The `SEXP` returned by `fun`.

args.fun: C function to call after context setup. Passed `*data`.
args.cleanfun: C function to call before context teardown. Passed `*data`.

notes:
Older, simpler variant of `R_UnwindProtect()`; the cleanup function is
not told whether the exit was a normal return or a longjmp.

name: R_tryCatchError
summary: Call a C function with a handler installed for R error conditions.
returns: The `SEXP` returned by `fun`, or the handler's return value if an error is signalled.

args.hndlr: handler called with the condition object; its return value becomes the result.

notes:
`R_tryCatchError()` installs an exiting handler (like
`tryCatch(error = ...)`); `R_withCallingErrorHandler()` installs a
calling handler (like `withCallingHandlers(error = ...)`) and avoids
calling back into R, so it is more efficient. `R_tryCatchError()` is
implemented via R-level `tryCatch()` and has some overhead.

name: R_tryCatch
summary: Call a C function with handlers for arbitrary condition classes and a cleanup action.
signature:
SEXP R_tryCatch(SEXP (*fun)(void *data), void *data,
                SEXP conds,
                SEXP (*hndlr)(SEXP cond, void *hdata), void *hdata,
                void (*clean)(void *cdata), void *cdata);
returns: The `SEXP` returned by `fun`, or the handler's return value if a handled condition is signalled.

args.conds: condition classes to handle, as a character vector (`STRSXP`).

notes:
`NULL` may be passed for `fun` or `clean` if condition handling or
cleanup is not needed. Implemented via R-level `tryCatch()`, so it has
some overhead.

name: R_CheckUserInterrupt
summary: Check for a pending user interrupt, signalling an error if one occurred.
notes:
Call periodically from long-running loops; R cannot interrupt compiled
code that never checks. On interrupt it longjmps, so the same cleanup
obligations as for `Rf_error()` apply.

name: R_CheckStack
summary: Signal an error if the C stack is (nearly) exhausted.

args.extra: `R_CheckStack2()` errors when fewer than `extra` bytes remain.

notes:
Call before deep C recursion; better still, avoid deep recursion or
write it tail-recursively so the compiler can optimize it away. Stack
checking is not available on all platforms.

name: UNIMPLEMENTED
summary: Signal an error for an unimplemented operation.
notes:
Signals "feature 's' is not implemented"; never returns. Use
`UNIMPLEMENTED_TYPE()` for a type-specific variant.

name: Rf_onintr
summary: R's default response to a user interrupt.
notes:
Jumps back to the top level, discarding the current computation.
Intended for front-ends and graphics devices; package code should
almost always use `R_CheckUserInterrupt()` instead.

name: Rf_eval
summary: Evaluate an expression in an environment.
returns: The result of evaluating `expression` in `environment`; may be `R_NilValue`.
notes: Expression can be anything - non-language objects are returned as is.

name: R_forceAndCall
summary: Force promises in an expression and then call it.
signature: SEXP R_forceAndCall(SEXP expression, int n, SEXP environment);
returns: The result of the call after forcing the first `n` arguments.

args.n: The number of arguments to force.

notes:
`n` is the number of leading arguments in the call to force before
evaluating.

name: R_tryEval
summary: Evaluate an R expression in a stand-alone context so errors don't longjmp.
signature:
SEXP R_tryEval(SEXP expression, SEXP environment, int* pOutError);
SEXP R_tryEvalSilent(SEXP expression, SEXP environment, int* pOutError);
returns: The result of evaluating `expression`, or `NULL` on error (with `*pOutError` set to 1).

args.pOutError: On error, the function returns NULL and sets the contents of `pOutError` to 1.

notes:
`R_tryEvalSilent()` behaves like `R_tryEval()` but suppresses printing
of error messages. Both ignore existing condition handlers, so R-level
`tryCatch()` and `suppressWarnings()` have no effect on the evaluation.

name: R_ToplevelExec
summary: Execute a C function in a top-level context, catching any errors.
returns: `TRUE` if `fun` ran to completion, `FALSE` if an error occurred.

args.fun: C function to call after context setup. Passed `*data`.

notes: Both `R_tryEval()` and `R_tryEvalSilent()` call `R_ToplevelExec` under the hood.

name: R_curErrorBuf
summary: Access the text of the current error.
returns: The text of the current error message.

name: Rf_substitute
summary: Substitute values for variables in an expression.
returns: The expression with variables replaced by their values.

name: R_ParseVector
summary: Parse R code from a character vector or C string.
returns: `R_ParseVector()` and `R_ParseString()` return an `EXPRSXP` vector of parsed expressions; `R_ParseEvalString()` returns the result of evaluating the parsed code in `env`.

args.text: a character vector of lines of R code.
args.n: number of elements to parse, or -1 for all.

notes:
Returns an `EXPRSXP` of parsed expressions. `R_ParseString()` (R
4.4.0) parses a single C string; `R_ParseEvalString()` parses and
evaluates in one step. Check `status` before evaluating the result.

name: R_MakeExternalPtr
summary: Create an external pointer wrapping a C pointer.
signature: SEXP R_MakeExternalPtr(void *p, SEXP tag, SEXP prot);
returns: A new external pointer (`EXTPTRSXP`) wrapping `p`.

name: R_ClearExternalPtr
summary: Clear the address stored in an external pointer.

name: R_ExternalPtrAddr
summary: Get and set the address, tag, and protected fields of an external pointer.
returns: `R_ExternalPtrAddr()` returns the stored C pointer; `R_ExternalPtrTag()` and `R_ExternalPtrProtected()` return the tag and protected fields.

name: R_RegisterCFinalizer
summary: Register a finalizer to run when an external pointer is garbage collected.
notes:
`R_RegisterFinalizer()` takes an R function and `R_RegisterCFinalizer()`
a C function of type `R_CFinalizer_t`. The `Ex` variants add an `onexit`
argument controlling whether the finalizer also runs when R shuts down.

name: R_MakeWeakRef
summary: Create a weak reference.
signature:
SEXP R_MakeWeakRef(SEXP key, SEXP val, SEXP fin, Rboolean onexit);
SEXP R_MakeWeakRefC(SEXP key, SEXP val, R_CFinalizer_t fin, Rboolean onexit);
returns: A newly created weak reference object.
notes:
`R_MakeWeakRef()` takes an R function finalizer; `R_MakeWeakRefC()` takes
a C finalizer of type `R_CFinalizer_t`.

name: R_WeakRefKey
summary: Get the key or value of a weak reference.
signature:
SEXP R_WeakRefKey(SEXP w);
SEXP R_WeakRefValue(SEXP w);
returns: `R_WeakRefKey()` returns the key and `R_WeakRefValue()` the value stored in `w`.

name: R_RunWeakRefFinalizer
summary: Run the finalizer attached to a weak reference.

name: R_MakeExternalPtrFn
summary: Wrap a C function pointer in an external pointer.
signature:
SEXP R_MakeExternalPtrFn(DL_FUNC p, SEXP tag, SEXP prot);
DL_FUNC R_ExternalPtrAddrFn(SEXP s);
returns: `R_MakeExternalPtrFn()` returns a new external pointer wrapping `p`; `R_ExternalPtrAddrFn()` returns the stored function pointer.

args.prot: an object to protect from GC while the pointer lives.

notes:
The function-pointer analogue of `R_MakeExternalPtr()`; storing a
`DL_FUNC` directly avoids casting between object and function
pointers, which is undefined behaviour in C.

name: Rf_isFunction
summary: Test whether an object is a function or a primitive function.
returns: `TRUE` if the object is a function (respectively a primitive function), otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: `FUNSXP` is an abstract union type.

name: R_UnboundValue
summary: Access the unbound-value marker constant.
notes: `R_UnboundValue` marks an unbound symbol or an unread promise value.

name: R_Srcref
summary: Access the current srcref, for debuggers.
signature: LibExtern SEXP	R_Srcref;           /* Current srcref, for debuggers */

name: R_GetCurrentSrcref
summary: Get the current srcref or the source filename of a srcref.
returns: `R_GetCurrentSrcref()` returns the current srcref, or `R_NilValue` if none; `R_GetSrcFilename()` returns the filename stored in a srcref.

name: R_mkClosure
summary: Create a closure from formals, body, and environment.
signature: SEXP R_mkClosure(SEXP formals, SEXP body, SEXP env);
returns: A new `CLOSXP` closure.
notes:
The API replacement for the non-API idiom `Rf_allocSExp(CLOSXP)` +
`SET_FORMALS`/`SET_BODY`/`SET_CLOENV`. Checks that `formals` is a
well-formed pairlist of formal arguments.

name: R_ClosureFormals
summary: Access the formals, body, or environment of a closure.
returns: The formals, body, or environment of closure `x`, respectively.
notes: The API replacements for `FORMALS()`, `BODY()`, and `CLOENV()`.

name: R_ClosureExpr
summary: Get the body expression of a closure.
returns: The unevaluated body expression of the closure.
notes: Returns the unevaluated body, like `body()` at the R level.

name: R_BytecodeExpr
summary: Get the byte-compiled form of a closure's body.
returns: The byte-compiled body as a `BCODESXP`, or `R_NilValue` if the closure is not byte-compiled.
notes:
Returns a `BCODESXP` if the closure has been byte-compiled, and
`R_NilValue` otherwise.

name: dnorm
summary: Density, CDF, quantile, and random generation for a distribution.
returns: The density, cumulative probability, quantile, or random draw as a double; `NaN` with a warning on invalid parameters.

args.give_log: return the result on the log scale.
args.lower_tail: use the lower (left) tail; set to 0 for the upper tail.
args.log_p: `p` is supplied on the log scale.

notes:
Shown for the normal distribution; every distribution in the table
above follows the same argument pattern with its own parameters. The
cumulative hazard is `-pdist(t, ..., 0, 1)`. The `r*` functions draw
from R's RNG stream and must be bracketed by
`GetRNGstate()`/`PutRNGstate()` (see [Random number
generation](rng.qmd)). With `R_NO_REMAP_RMATH` defined, the normal
names become `Rf_dnorm4`, `Rf_pnorm5`, `Rf_qnorm5`.

name: dnbinom_mu
summary: Negative binomial distribution in the alternative (size, mu) parametrization.
returns: The density, cumulative probability, quantile, or random draw as a double; `NaN` with a warning on invalid parameters.

name: dbinom_raw
summary: Binomial and Poisson mass functions that vary continuously in x.
signature:
double dbinom_raw(double x, double n, double p, double q, int give_log);
double dpois_raw(double x, double lambda, int give_log);
returns: The probability mass at `x` (or its log when `give_log` is nonzero) as a double.
notes:
Unlike `dbinom()`/`dpois()`, these return nonzero values for
non-integer `x`. `dbinom_raw()` takes both `p` and `q = 1 - p`, which
is more accurate when one is close to 1.

name: Rf_rmultinom
summary: Generate one multinomial random vector.
signature:
void Rf_rmultinom(int n, double* prob, int K, int* rN);
#define rmultinom Rf_rmultinom

args.n: number of trials; the counts in `rN` sum to `n`.
args.prob: length-`K` vector of probabilities, summing to 1.
args.rN: output: length-`K` integer array filled with the counts.

notes: Must be bracketed by `GetRNGstate()`/`PutRNGstate()`.

name: wilcox_free
summary: Free memory cached by the Wilcoxon distribution functions.
notes:
Call after any use of `dwilcox`/`pwilcox`/`qwilcox` (or the
`signrank` equivalents). Declared in `Rmath.h` only from R 4.2.0; for
earlier versions declare `extern void wilcox_free(void);` yourself.
These names are never remapped.

name: gammafn
summary: Gamma function, its log, and derivatives of the digamma function.
returns: The function value at `x` as a double; `NaN` with a warning on domain errors.
notes:
`digamma(x)` is `psigamma(x, 0)`, `trigamma(x)` is `psigamma(x, 1)`,
and so on. When you need several derivatives at once, the underlying
workhorse `dpsifn()` computes a whole sequence in one call; see
`src/nmath/polygamma.c` in the R sources.

name: beta
summary: Beta function and its natural logarithm.
signature:
double beta(double a, double b);
double lbeta(double a, double b);
returns: `beta()` returns the value of the beta function and `lbeta()` its natural logarithm, both as a double; `NaN` with a warning if `a` or `b` is negative.

name: choose
summary: Binomial coefficient and its log, generalized to real n.
signature:
double choose(double n, double k);
double lchoose(double n, double k);
returns: The binomial coefficient (or its natural logarithm) as a double; 0 when `k < 0`.
notes: `k` is rounded to the nearest integer (with a warning if needed).

name: bessel_i
summary: Bessel functions I, J, K, and Y of fractional order.
returns: The value of the Bessel function at `x` (exponentially scaled if requested) as a double; `NaN` with a warning on domain errors.

args.expo: for `bessel_i`/`bessel_k` only: 1 for unscaled, 2 to return `exp(-x) * I(x, nu)` or `exp(x) * K(x, nu)` (avoids overflow).

name: R_pow
summary: Exponentiation with R's edge-case semantics.
returns: `x` raised to the power `y` with R's `^` edge-case semantics (`pow1p()` computes `(1 + x)^y`), as a double.
notes:
Unlike C's `pow()`, these give the same result as R's `^` when `x` or
`y` is 0, missing, infinite, or `NaN`. `pow1p(x, y)` computes
`(1 + x)^y` accurately for small `|x|`.

name: log1pmx
summary: Accurate log computations in numerically delicate regions.
returns: The computed value as a double; `NaN` with a warning outside the domain.
notes:
Respectively `log(1 + x) - x` (accurate for small `|x|`),
`log(1 + exp(x))` (accurate for large `x`), `log(1 - exp(-x))`, and
`log(gamma(x + 1))` (accurate for `0 < x < 0.5`). Prefer these over
composing the naive expressions.

name: cospi
summary: Trigonometric functions of pi * x, accurate at (half-)integer x.
returns: The value of the function at `x * pi` as a double; `NaN` where the function is undefined.
notes:
Prefer `Rtanpi()` over `tanpi()`: `Rtanpi()` is always R's own
implementation (exactly ±1 at quarter integers, `NaN` at half
integers), while `tanpi()` may be the platform's, with
platform-dependent behaviour at half and quarter integers.

name: logspace_add
summary: Add, subtract, or sum values given on the log scale.
returns: The result on the log scale as a double, e.g. `log(exp(logx) + exp(logy))`.
notes:
Compute `log(exp(logx) + exp(logy))` etc. without overflow or
unnecessary loss of accuracy — the building blocks for working in
log-space.

name: fmax2
summary: Maximum and minimum of two doubles or ints.
returns: The larger (`fmax2()`/`imax2()`) or smaller (`fmin2()`/`imin2()`) of the two arguments; `NaN` if either is `NaN`.
notes:
Unlike C99's `fmax()`/`fmin()`, these return `NaN` when either
argument is `NaN`.

name: sign
summary: Signum function and transfer of sign.
signature:
double sign(double x);
double fsign(double x, double y);
returns: `sign()` returns 1, 0, -1, or `NaN` for `NaN` input; `fsign()` returns `|x|` with the sign of `y`.
notes:
`sign()` returns 1, 0, −1, or `NaN` for `NaN`. `fsign(x, y)` is
`|x| * sign(y)`.

name: fround
summary: Rounding used by R's round() and signif().
returns: The rounded (`fround()`/`fprec()`) or truncated (`ftrunc()`) value as a double.

name: M_PI
summary: Mathematical constants defined to at least 30 digits.
notes:
See the table above for the full set. The S-compatibility constant
`PI` is defunct; use `M_PI`. `R_ext/Constants.h` additionally
includes `float.h`/`cfloat` for `DBL_MAX` and friends.

name: expm1
summary: Compute exp(x) - 1 and log(1 + x) accurately for small x.
signature:
double expm1(double x);
double log1p(double x);
returns: The value of `exp(x) - 1` or `log(1 + x)` as a double.
notes:
C99 functions that R requires; `Rmath.h` remaps `log1p()` to R's own
implementation on platforms where the system version is inaccurate.

name: dpsifn
summary: Compute derivatives of the log-gamma (psi) function.
signature: void dpsifn(double x, int n, int kode, int m, double *ans, int *nz, int *ierr);

args.m: number of sequence values to compute.
args.ans: output array of length at least m.

notes:
Low-level workhorse behind `digamma()`/`trigamma()`; most code
should call `digamma()` etc. directly.

name: R_alloc
summary: Allocate temporary memory that R reclaims automatically.
signature:
char* R_alloc(size_t, int);
long double *R_allocLD(size_t nelem);
returns: A pointer to the allocated memory, freed automatically when the `.Call` entry point returns.
notes:
Memory is freed automatically when the `.Call` entry point returns
(including on error or interrupt). `R_allocLD()` additionally
guarantees the 16-byte alignment some platforms need for
`long double`.

name: S_alloc
summary: Allocate and reallocate temporary memory using the legacy S interface.
signature:
char* S_alloc(long, int);
char* S_realloc(char *, long, long, int);
returns: A pointer to the allocated (or reallocated) temporary memory.
notes:
Best avoided: `long` is limited to 2^31 - 1 bytes on 64-bit Windows,
so these cannot handle large allocations there. Prefer `R_alloc()`.

name: vmaxget
summary: Get and set the high-water mark of R's temporary allocation arena.
returns: `vmaxget()` returns the current allocation high-water mark, for passing back to `vmaxset()`.
notes:
`vmaxset()` releases everything allocated by `R_alloc()` since the
matching `vmaxget()`. Useful to bound memory growth when calling
`R_alloc()` in a loop, but easy to get wrong — for experts only.

name: R_Calloc
summary: Allocate, reallocate, and free user-controlled memory with R error handling.
returns: `R_Calloc()` and `R_Realloc()` return a pointer to the allocated memory; never `NULL`, since failure raises an R error.
notes:
Analogues of `calloc()`/`realloc()`/`free()`; on allocation failure R
throws an error, so a returned pointer is always valid. You must
`R_Free()` on every path, including error paths (see
`R_UnwindProtect()`). Never mix with `malloc()`/`free()`, and never
call the underlying `R_chk_calloc()` etc. directly. The legacy
`Calloc`/`Realloc`/`Free` spellings were removed in R 4.5.0.

name: R_malloc_gc
summary: Allocate memory, retrying after a garbage collection on failure.
returns: A pointer to the allocated memory, or `NULL` if allocation fails even after a garbage collection.
notes:
Like `malloc()`/`calloc()`/`realloc()`, but if the allocation fails
a garbage collection is run and the allocation retried. Memory must
be released with `free()`.

name: nmmin
summary: Minimize a function using the code underlying optim().
signature:
void nmmin(int n, double *xin, double *x, double *Fmin, optimfn fn,
           int *fail, double abstol, double intol, void *ex,
           double alpha, double beta, double gamma, int trace,
           int *fncount, int maxit);
void vmmin(int n, double *x, double *Fmin,
           optimfn fn, optimgr gr, int maxit, int trace,
           int *mask, double abstol, double reltol, int nREPORT,
           void *ex, int *fncount, int *grcount, int *fail);
void cgmin(int n, double *xin, double *x, double *Fmin,
           optimfn fn, optimgr gr, int *fail, double abstol,
           double intol, void *ex, int type, int trace,
           int *fncount, int *grcount, int maxit);
void lbfgsb(int n, int lmm, double *x, double *lower,
            double *upper, int *nbd, double *Fmin, optimfn fn,
            optimgr gr, int *fail, void *ex, double factr,
            double pgtol, int *fncount, int *grcount,
            int maxit, char *msg, int trace, int nREPORT);
void samin(int n, double *x, double *Fmin, optimfn fn, int maxit,
           int tmax, double temp, int trace, void *ex);
notes:
Respectively Nelder–Mead, BFGS, conjugate gradients, limited-memory
BFGS with box constraints, and simulated annealing. Common arguments:
`n` is the number of parameters, `x`/`xin` hold the starting
parameters on entry and `x` the result on exit, `Fmin` receives the
final value, `fail` is a nonzero-on-failure flag, and `fncount`/
`grcount` report evaluation counts. See `?optim` for the remaining
arguments and `src/appl/lbfgsb.c` for the `nbd` bounds codes. No
finite-differencing or Hessian approximation is provided. (`optif9`,
also declared here, is experimental and intended only for the nlme
package.)

name: Rdqags
summary: Numerically integrate a function over a finite or infinite interval.
signature:
void Rdqags(integr_fn f, void *ex, double *a, double *b,
            double *epsabs, double *epsrel,
            double *result, double *abserr, int *neval, int *ier,
            int *limit, int *lenw, int *last,
            int *iwork, double *work);
void Rdqagi(integr_fn f, void *ex, double *bound, int *inf,
            double *epsabs, double *epsrel,
            double *result, double *abserr, int *neval, int *ier,
            int *limit, int *lenw, int *last,
            int *iwork, double *work);

args.bound: `Rdqagi`: the finite bound, with `inf` selecting the range: 1 for `(bound, Inf)`, −1 for `(-Inf, bound)`, 2 for `(-Inf, Inf)`.
args.result: outputs: value, absolute error estimate, evaluation count, error code, and number of subdivisions (`result`, `abserr`, `neval`, `ier`, `last`).
args.limit: maximum number of subintervals, as `subdivisions` in `integrate()`.

notes:
Always allocate the work arrays as `iwork = R_alloc(limit,
sizeof(int))` and `work = R_alloc(lenw, sizeof(double))` with
`lenw = 4 * limit`. The comments in `src/appl/integrate.c` explain
the `ier` failure codes.

name: dqrdc2
summary: LINPACK-derived QR decomposition and least-squares routines.
signature:
void F77_NAME(dqrdc2)(double *x, int *ldx, int *n, int *p,
                      double *tol, int *rank,
                      double *qraux, int *pivot, double *work);
void F77_NAME(dqrls)(double *x, int *n, int *p, double *y, int *ny,
                     double *tol, double *b, double *rsd,
                     double *qty, int *k,
                     int *jpvt, double *qraux, double *work);
notes:
These Fortran routines underlie `lm.fit()`, `lm.wfit()`, and
`qr(LAPACK = FALSE)`; `dqrdc2` is R's modification of LINPACK's
`dqrdc` with column pivoting and rank computation. Prefer BLAS/LAPACK
for new code; see the sources in `src/appl/` for argument details.
Regarded as API for now, but may be replaced by `bind(C)` interfaces
in future.

name: findInterval
summary: Locate the interval containing a value within a sorted vector.
returns: The index of the interval in `xt` containing `x`, from 0 (below the first breakpoint) to `n`.
notes:
Also declared in `R_ext/Applic.h`. `findInterval2()` adds a
`left_open` argument for left-open intervals. `interv` is the
Fortran-callable predecessor, declared only under `R_RS_H`. The
algorithm is fastest when `ilo` carries the previous result and
successive `x` values are monotone.

name: R_max_col
summary: Find the column position of the maximum in each row of a matrix.
signature: void R_max_col(double *matrix, int *nr, int *nc, int *maxes, int *ties_meth);
notes: Also declared in `R_ext/Applic.h`.

name: d1mach
summary: Report machine floating-point or integer constants.
returns: `d1mach()` returns the requested floating-point machine constant; `i1mach()` returns the requested integer machine constant.
notes:
Fortran-era routines kept for old numerical code. New code should
use the C99 constants from `<float.h>`/`<limits.h>` or
`R_ext/Arith.h` instead.

name: Rf_isObject
summary: Test whether an object is flagged as object-oriented.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` has the object bit set (i.e. carries a class attribute), otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
Returns non-zero when the `OBJECT` bit is set on `s`, i.e. the object
carries a class attribute.

name: Rf_inherits
summary: Test whether an object inherits from a given class.
returns: `TRUE` if the object inherits from the named class, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Matches the given name against the object's class attribute.

name: Rf_S3Class
summary: Return the S3 class of an object.
returns: A character vector `SEXP` of the object's S3 class names.
notes: Returns a character vector of class names.

name: Rf_isBasicClass
summary: Test whether a class name is one of the basic classes.
returns: Non-zero if the name is one of the basic classes, zero otherwise.
notes: Basic classes are the built-in pseudo-classes (e.g. `"numeric"`, `"matrix"`) known to the methods package.

name: Rf_classgets
summary: Set the class attribute of an object.
returns: The object with its class attribute set to the second argument.

name: Rf_isS4
summary: Test whether an object is an S4 object.
returns: `TRUE` if the object is an S4 object, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Returns non-zero for objects of type `S4SXP`.

name: Rf_asS4
summary: Set or unset the S4 flag on an object.
returns: The (possibly duplicated) object with its S4 flag set or unset.

name: Rf_allocS4Object
summary: Allocate a new S4 object.
returns: A newly allocated bare S4 object (`S4SXP`).
notes: Allocates a bare S4 object (type `S4SXP`) with the S4 flag set.

name: R_S4_extends
summary: Query S4 class inheritance (extends) relationships.
signature:
SEXP R_S4_extends(SEXP klass, SEXP useTable);
Rboolean R_extends(SEXP class1, SEXP class2, SEXP env);
returns: `R_S4_extends()` returns a `SEXP` describing the superclasses of `klass`; `R_extends()` returns `TRUE` if `class1` extends `class2`, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: R_do_MAKE_CLASS
summary: Create a new S4 class definition.
returns: The newly created S4 class definition `SEXP`.

name: R_getClassDef
summary: Retrieve an S4 class definition by name.
signature:
SEXP R_getClassDef(const char *what);
SEXP R_getClassDef_R(SEXP what);
returns: The S4 class definition `SEXP` for the named class.
notes:
`R_getClassDef_R()` takes the class name as a `SEXP` rather than a C
string.

name: R_has_methods_attached
summary: Test whether methods are currently attached.
returns: `TRUE` if methods are currently attached, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: R_isVirtualClass
summary: Test whether an S4 class definition describes a virtual class.
returns: `TRUE` if the class definition describes a virtual class, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: R_do_new_object
summary: Create a new object from an S4 class definition.
returns: A new instance `SEXP` of the S4 class.

name: R_check_class_and_super
summary: Check an object against a set of valid classes, a C-level `is()`.
signature:
int R_check_class_and_super(SEXP x, const char **valid, SEXP rho);
int R_check_class_etc(SEXP x, const char **valid);
returns: The 0-based index of the matching class in `valid`, or `-1` if `x` matches none of them.
notes:
Checks whether `x` matches or extends one of the classes in the
`NULL`-terminated array `valid`. `R_check_class_etc()` omits the
environment argument.

name: R_do_slot
summary: Get, assign, or test for the presence of an S4 slot.
returns: `R_do_slot()` returns the slot's value; `R_do_slot_assign()` returns the object with the slot assigned; `R_has_slot()` returns non-zero if the slot exists.
notes:
`R_do_slot()` extracts a slot, `R_do_slot_assign()` assigns it, and
`R_has_slot()` tests for its presence.

name: Rf_isPairList
summary: Test whether an object is a pairlist, a call, or a pairlist-or-NULL.
signature:
Rboolean Rf_isPairList(SEXP x); // LISTSXP
Rboolean Rf_isLanguage(SEXP x); // LANGSXP
Rboolean Rf_isList(SEXP x);     // LISTSXP, NILSXP
returns: `TRUE` when `x` passes the test — a pairlist for `Rf_isPairList()`, a call for `Rf_isLanguage()`, a pairlist or `NULL` for `Rf_isList()`; otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_cons
summary: Create a new CONS cell linking two objects.
signature:
SEXP Rf_cons(SEXP a, SEXP b);   // function arguments
SEXP Rf_lcons(SEXP a, SEXP b);  // calls
returns: A freshly allocated cell with `CAR` set to `a` and `CDR` to `b`: a `LISTSXP` from `Rf_cons()`, a `LANGSXP` from `Rf_lcons()`.
notes: The `CDR` of the final value must be `R_NilValue`.

name: Rf_list1
summary: Create a pairlist of one to six elements.
returns: A freshly allocated pairlist of one to six elements, terminated by `R_NilValue`.
notes: These automatically add the terminating `R_NilValue`.

name: Rf_lang1
summary: Create a call to a function with zero to five arguments.
returns: A freshly allocated call (`LANGSXP`) to function `x1` with the given arguments, terminated by `R_NilValue`.
notes: These automatically add the terminating `R_NilValue`.

name: Rf_allocFormalsList2
summary: Allocate a formals pairlist of two to six elements.
returns: A freshly allocated formals pairlist of two to six elements, tagged with the given symbols.
notes: These automatically add the terminating `R_NilValue`.

name: Rf_PairToVectorList
summary: Convert a pairlist to a list vector, or a list vector to a pairlist.
signature:
SEXP Rf_PairToVectorList(SEXP x);
SEXP Rf_VectorToPairList(SEXP x);
returns: A freshly allocated copy of `x` converted to a list vector (`Rf_PairToVectorList()`) or a pairlist (`Rf_VectorToPairList()`).

name: Rf_listAppend
summary: Append one pairlist to another.
returns: The mutated `source` pairlist, now with `target` appended; no new cells are allocated.
notes:
Mutates `source` in place by walking to its last cell and setting its
`CDR` to `target`; no new cells are allocated and the returned pairlist
is the (mutated) `source` you already hold.

name: CAR
summary: Get the first element or a nested component of a CONS cell.
returns: The requested component of cell `e` — a pointer into the existing structure, not a copy.
notes:
Pairlists can't be indexed directly, so these accessors navigate the
linked list instead. `CAR()` returns the first element and `CDR()` the
rest; they compose to give `CAAR()`, `CDAR()`, `CADDR()`, `CADDDR()`, and
so on.

name: SETCAR
summary: Set the first element or a nested component of a CONS cell.
returns: The assigned value `y`; the cell is modified in place.
notes: Mirror the `CAR()`/`CDR()` family of getters.

name: TAG
summary: Get or set the tag (name) attached to a node of a pairlist.
signature:
SEXP TAG(SEXP e);
void SET_TAG(SEXP x, SEXP y);
returns: `TAG()` returns the tag (name) attached to node `e`, or `R_NilValue` if it has none.

name: MISSING
summary: Test whether a pairlist element is a missing argument.
returns: Non-zero if `x` is a missing argument, `0` otherwise.
notes: `SET_MISSING()` was removed from the headers in R 4.6.0.

name: Rf_allocList
summary: Create a new pairlist of the specified length.
returns: A freshly allocated pairlist of length `n` with all elements `R_NilValue`.
notes:
Treats the pairlist as if it were a vector, which is easy to get O(n^2)
from, but is unlikely to be a bottleneck at typical pairlist sizes. To
create a call expression, use `Rf_allocLang()` (added in R 4.4.1) or
`Rf_lcons()` rather than `Rf_allocList()` plus `SET_TYPEOF()`, which
will not be available to packages in the future.

name: Rf_nthcdr
summary: Access the nth element of a pairlist.
returns: The tail of `x` after `n` `CDR`s — a pointer into the existing pairlist, not a copy.
notes:
Treats the pairlist as if it were a vector; repeated calls can become
O(n^2), though this is unlikely to matter at typical pairlist sizes.
Errors if `x` is not a pairlist or has fewer than `n` elements.

name: Rf_elt
summary: Get an element of a pairlist by index, or the last element.
returns: `Rf_elt()` returns the element of the pairlist at the given index and `Rf_lastElt()` the last element; both are pointers into the existing structure, not copies.

name: Rf_isUserBinop
summary: Test whether a call is a user-defined binary operator.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` is a call to a user-defined binary operator (`%...%`), otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_allocLang
summary: Allocate a call (LANGSXP) with room for a function and n - 1 arguments.
returns: A freshly allocated call (`LANGSXP`) with `n` nodes, all elements initially `R_NilValue`.

args.n: total number of pairlist nodes (function plus arguments).

notes:
The API replacement for the non-API idiom `Rf_allocList(n)` +
`SET_TYPEOF(..., LANGSXP)`. Fill in the function and arguments with
`SETCAR()`/`SETCADR()` etc. before evaluating.

name: CONS
summary: Prepend an element to a pairlist or call.
signature:
#define CONS(a, b)  Rf_cons((a), (b))
#define LCONS(a, b) Rf_lcons((a), (b))
notes:
Macro aliases for `Rf_cons()`/`Rf_lcons()`; the `Rf_` forms are
preferred in new code.

name: R_ShowMessage
summary: Display a message to the user.

name: Rprintf
summary: Print to R's output or error stream.
notes:
Unlike `printf()`, output goes to R's console: it respects `sink()`
redirection and appears in GUIs and on cluster nodes. Write complete
lines (ending in `\n`) before returning to R. The `v` variants take a
`va_list`; in C++ code they require C++11 or `R_USE_C99_IN_CXX`.

name: Rf_PrintValue
summary: Print an object like print() would.

name: IndexWidth
summary: Compute the character width needed to print a vector index.

name: R_gc
summary: Trigger garbage collection, or check whether it is running.
returns: `R_gc_running()` returns non-zero while garbage collection is running, zero otherwise.

name: Rf_protect
summary: Protect and unprotect objects from garbage collection.
returns: `Rf_protect()` returns its argument, the protected `SEXP`.
notes:
These are the underlying functions for the `PROTECT()` and `UNPROTECT()`
macros; use the macros instead in package code.

name: R_ProtectWithIndex
summary: Protect an object at a fixed stack location so its value can be replaced later.
signature:
void R_ProtectWithIndex(SEXP, PROTECT_INDEX *);
void R_Reprotect(SEXP, PROTECT_INDEX);
notes:
These are the underlying functions for the `PROTECT_WITH_INDEX()` and
`REPROTECT()` macros. Useful when you need to coerce a protected value
and replace it in place, such as inside a loop.

name: R_PreserveObject
summary: Preserve an object across C calls by adding it to R's precious list.
notes:
Objects are added to `R_PreciousList`, a pairlist walked by the garbage
collector. `R_PreserveObject()` allocates (it conses the object onto
`R_PreciousList`), so it can throw on out-of-memory; `R_ReleaseObject()`
performs a linear search of this list to remove the entry and does not
allocate, but repeatedly preserving and releasing many objects in the
same order can cause quadratic slowdowns.

name: MAYBE_SHARED
summary: Test or set an object's reference-count flags before modifying it in place.
returns: `MAYBE_SHARED()` returns non-zero if `x` may be referenced more than once; `NO_REFERENCES()` returns non-zero if `x` has no references (the `MAYBE_REFERENCED()` and `NOT_SHARED()` macros return the negations).
notes:
Package code sees these as plain functions, not macros (that expansion
is only visible inside R's own build, where `USE_RINTERNALS` is
defined). By default they test the `REFCNT` reference count, since R
defines `SWITCH_TO_REFCNT` unless a package opts out with
`SWITCH_TO_NAMED`; the legacy `NAMED` counter is what they test in that
(rare) opt-out case.

name: Rf_duplicate
summary: Duplicate an object, either deeply or shallowly.
returns: A copy of the input `SEXP` — deep for `Rf_duplicate()`, shallow for `Rf_shallow_duplicate()`; `Rf_lazy_duplicate()` returns the input itself, marked so it is copied before modification.
notes:
Use `Rf_shallow_duplicate()` for lists when only the top-level structure
needs copying; `Rf_duplicate()` also copies every element.

name: TYPEOF
summary: Read an object's type tag and header flags.
returns: `TYPEOF()` returns the `SEXPTYPE` tag of `x`; `NAMED()` and `REFCNT()` return the corresponding header fields.
notes:
`TYPEOF()` is the canonical way to test an object's type. The flag
accessors are mostly needed only for the reference-count checks
described above. There are no API setters for the type or object
flags — use constructors (e.g. `Rf_allocLang()`) and `Rf_setAttrib()`
instead.

name: PROTECT
summary: Protect SEXPs from garbage collection.
returns: `PROTECT()` returns `s`; `PROTECT_WITH_INDEX()` returns a `PROTECT_INDEX` token for use with `REPROTECT()`.
notes:
`PROTECT()` pushes `s` onto the protection stack; `UNPROTECT(n)` pops the
`n` most recent entries. Unbalanced use inside a loop can overflow the
protection stack, since it is only reset automatically when your `.Call`
entry point returns. Use `PROTECT_WITH_INDEX()`/`REPROTECT()` to re-protect
a different value at the same stack depth, e.g. inside a loop.

name: R_NewPreciousMSet
summary: Protect a changing set of objects across R calls.
returns: A new precious multi-set `SEXP`, which itself needs protection.
notes:
A "precious multi-set" protects many objects more cheaply than one
`R_PreserveObject()` per object. The set itself must be protected
(e.g. with `R_PreserveObject()`); members can be added and removed
freely.

name: UNPROTECT_PTR
summary: Unprotect a specific object by pointer.
notes:
Searches the protection stack for a matching entry and removes it,
rather than unprotecting the most recent entries. Convenient but
error-prone: prefer a strict `PROTECT`/`UNPROTECT` stack discipline,
or `PROTECT_WITH_INDEX` when the number of protected objects varies.

name: R_Version
summary: Test the compile-time version of R against a required version.
notes:
`R_VERSION` is the packed version number of the R being compiled
against; `R_Version()` packs a `major.minor.patch` triple into the
same format for comparison.

name: GetRNGstate
summary: Read in (or create) `.Random.seed` before generating variates, and write it back after.
notes:
Every use of R's RNG from C must be bracketed by these calls:
`GetRNGstate()` reads (or lazily creates) `.Random.seed`, and
`PutRNGstate()` writes the updated state back so R-level code sees the
stream advance. They can allocate when the seed doesn't yet exist.
These names are never remapped.

name: unif_rand
summary: Draw one uniform, standard normal, or unit exponential variate.
returns: One variate: uniform on (0, 1) for `unif_rand()`, standard normal for `norm_rand()`, unit exponential for `exp_rand()`.
notes:
Must be called between `GetRNGstate()` and `PutRNGstate()`. The
generator kind and seed are chosen at the R level (`RNGkind()`,
`set.seed()`); there is no C API to select them. For other
distributions, use the `r*` functions from `Rmath.h` (see
[Mathematical functions](math.qmd)) — they need the same bracketing.
These names are never remapped.

name: R_unif_index
summary: Draw a uniform index in `[0, n)` for random sampling.
returns: A uniform draw in `[0, n)`; truncate to an integer type to get an index.

args.n: upper bound (exclusive) on the returned index.

notes:
Returns a `double` in `[0, n)`; truncate to `int` or `R_xlen_t` to get
an index. Uses the sampling algorithm selected by R's
`sample.kind` option, so results match R-level `sample.int()`. Must be
called between `GetRNGstate()` and `PutRNGstate()`.

name: R_sample_kind
summary: Get the current discrete-sampling algorithm.
returns: The current sampling algorithm, `ROUNDING` or `REJECTION`.
notes:
Returns `ROUNDING` or `REJECTION`, reflecting the `sample.kind`
option; only relevant to code implementing its own discrete
sampling.

name: R_XDR_DOUBLE_SIZE
summary: Specify the byte sizes of doubles and integers in XDR serialisation format.

name: R_XDREncodeDouble
summary: Encode and decode doubles and integers in XDR format.
returns: `R_XDRDecodeDouble()` and `R_XDRDecodeInteger()` return the value decoded from `buf`.

name: R_InitInPStream
summary: Initialise a custom input or output persistence stream.
signature:
void R_InitInPStream(R_inpstream_t stream, R_pstream_data_t data,
  R_pstream_format_t type,
  int (*inchar)(R_inpstream_t),
  void (*inbytes)(R_inpstream_t, void *, int),
  SEXP (*phook)(SEXP, SEXP), SEXP pdata);
void R_InitOutPStream(R_outpstream_t stream, R_pstream_data_t data,
  R_pstream_format_t type, int version,
  void (*outchar)(R_outpstream_t, int),
  void (*outbytes)(R_outpstream_t, void *, int),
  SEXP (*phook)(SEXP, SEXP), SEXP pdata);

name: R_InitFileInPStream
summary: Initialise a persistence stream that reads from or writes to a file.

name: R_Serialize
summary: Serialise an R object to an output stream, or unserialise it from an input stream.
signature:
void R_Serialize(SEXP s, R_outpstream_t ops);
SEXP R_Unserialize(R_inpstream_t ips);
returns: `R_Unserialize()` returns the unserialised object; freshly allocated and unprotected.
notes:
The `SEXP` returned by `R_Unserialize()` is freshly allocated and must
be protected from garbage collection.

name: cetype_t
summary: Enumerate the encodings a CHARSXP can carry.
notes:
One of `CE_NATIVE`, `CE_UTF8`, `CE_LATIN1`, `CE_BYTES`, `CE_SYMBOL`, or
`CE_ANY`.

name: Rf_getCharCE
summary: Get the encoding of a CHARSXP.
returns: The encoding of the CHARSXP as a `cetype_t` value.

name: Rf_mkChar
summary: Create a CHARSXP from a C string in the current encoding.
signature:
SEXP Rf_mkChar(const char* x);
SEXP Rf_mkCharLen(const char* x, int n);
returns: The interned `CHARSXP` for the string as a `SEXP`; R's string cache means identical inputs return the same object.
notes:
`Rf_mkChar()` takes a null-terminated string; `Rf_mkCharLen()` takes an
explicit length. Protection is rarely needed since the result is usually
assigned immediately into a `STRSXP`. Both crash R on `NULL` input, so
check for it yourself and substitute `""` or `NA_STRING`.

name: Rf_mkCharCE
summary: Create a CHARSXP from a C string in a specified encoding.
signature:
SEXP Rf_mkCharCE(const char* x, cetype_t encoding);
SEXP Rf_mkCharLenCE(const char* x, int n, cetype_t encoding);
returns: The interned `CHARSXP` for the string in the requested encoding as a `SEXP`.
notes:
Prefer these over `Rf_mkChar()` and `Rf_mkString()` when the input is
UTF-8, which is typical for modern C code.

name: Rf_ScalarString
summary: Create a length-1 STRSXP from a CHARSXP or C string.
returns: A freshly allocated length-1 `STRSXP` as a `SEXP`.
notes:
`Rf_ScalarString()` builds a `STRSXP` from a `CHARSXP`; `Rf_mkString()`
builds one from a C string. Both crash R on `NULL` input.

name: CHAR
summary: Access the underlying C string stored in a CHARSXP.
signature:
const char* R_CHAR(SEXP x);
#define CHAR(x) R_CHAR(x)
returns: A pointer to the null-terminated C string stored inside the CHARSXP; owned by R, so do not modify or free it.
notes:
Named `CHAR()` for consistency with the other vector accessors
(`LOGICAL()`, `INTEGER()`, ...).

name: Rf_translateCharUTF8
summary: Translate a CHARSXP to a C string in a specified encoding.
returns: A pointer to the translated null-terminated C string; re-encoded results are allocated with `R_alloc()` and freed automatically at the end of the call.
notes:
`Rf_translateChar()` translates to the native encoding;
`Rf_translateChar0()` leaves bytes-encoded strings alone and otherwise
translates to native; `Rf_translateCharUTF8()` translates to UTF-8, which
is what most modern C APIs want. A re-encoded `char*` is allocated with
`R_alloc()` and freed automatically after the `.C`/`.Call`/`.External`
returns; copy it if you need to keep it longer.

name: NA_STRING
summary: Use the singleton CHARSXP representing NA.
signature:
SEXP R_NaString; // Singleton CHARSXP
#define NA_STRING R_NaString
notes: `R_NaString` is a singleton `CHARSXP`; `NA_STRING` is the macro alias.

name: R_BlankString
summary: Use the global blank string objects.
signature:
SEXP R_BlankString; // CHARSXP
SEXP R_BlankScalarString; // STRSXP
notes: `R_BlankString` is a `CHARSXP`; `R_BlankScalarString` is a `STRSXP`.

name: Rf_StringBlank
summary: Check whether a string is blank.
returns: `TRUE` if the string is empty (length zero), otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
`Rf_StringBlank()` takes a `SEXP`; `Rf_isBlankString()` takes a
`const char*`.

name: Rf_isValidString
summary: Check whether a STRSXP holds at least one valid string.
returns: `TRUE` if the validity condition described in the notes holds, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
`Rf_isValidString(x)` is `TYPEOF(x) == STRSXP && LENGTH(x) > 0 &&
TYPEOF(STRING_ELT(x, 0)) != NILSXP`; `Rf_isValidStringF(x)` is
`isValidString(x) && CHAR(STRING_ELT(x, 0))[0]`.

name: R_nchar
summary: Compute the length of a string in bytes, characters, or display width.
returns: The string length in bytes, characters, or display width as an `int`; `NA_INTEGER` for `NA_STRING` when `keepNA` is true.
notes:
Removed from the headers in R 4.6.0. There is no direct API
replacement; call `nchar()` at the R level, or count characters
yourself after `Rf_translateCharUTF8()`.

name: Rf_acopy_string
summary: Copy a C string into memory allocated by R_alloc().
returns: A pointer to a copy of the string allocated with `R_alloc()`; freed automatically, so do not free it.
notes: The copy is freed automatically at the next garbage collection.

name: Rf_asChar
summary: Render an R object to a CHARSXP.
returns: A `CHARSXP` rendering of `x` as a `SEXP`, as `as.character()` would produce it.

name: Rf_NonNullStringMatch
summary: Check that two strings are equal and neither NA nor empty.
returns: `TRUE` if the two strings are equal and neither is `NA_STRING` nor empty, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Translates both strings to UTF-8 before comparing.

name: Rf_reEnc
summary: Re-encode a C string from one encoding to another.
signature: const char *Rf_reEnc(const char *x, cetype_t ce_in, cetype_t ce_out, int subst);
returns: A pointer to the re-encoded null-terminated string; this may be `x` itself or an internal buffer, so copy it if it must outlive the call.

name: Rf_str2type
summary: Convert a C string to a SEXPTYPE.
returns: The `SEXPTYPE` named by the string, or `(SEXPTYPE) -1` if the name is not recognised.

name: Rf_type2str
summary: Convert a SEXPTYPE to a string.
returns: `Rf_type2char()` returns a static C string naming the type; `Rf_type2str()` and `Rf_type2str_nowarn()` return a `CHARSXP`; `Rf_type2rstr()` returns a length-1 `STRSXP`.
notes:
`Rf_type2char()` returns a C string; `Rf_type2rstr()` returns a
`STRSXP`; `Rf_type2str()` returns a `CHARSXP`. Only the `SEXP`-returning
members need protection.

name: Rf_pmatch
summary: Perform partial matching of strings.
signature:
Rboolean Rf_pmatch(SEXP, SEXP, Rboolean);
Rboolean Rf_psmatch(const char *, const char *, Rboolean);
returns: `TRUE` if the string matches the target exactly, or partially when partial matching is allowed; otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: `Rf_psmatch()` is the variant for C strings.

name: Rf_stringPositionTr
summary: Find the position of a string within a character vector.
returns: The 1-based index of the string in the vector, or -1 if not found.

name: Riconv
summary: Convert a string between encodings.
returns: `Riconv_open()` returns a conversion handle (`NULL` on failure); `Riconv()` returns the number of irreversible conversions performed, or `(size_t) -1` on error; `Riconv_close()` returns 0 on success.
notes:
A wrapper over the system `iconv()`, with the same calling
convention. `""` as an encoding name means the current native
encoding; `"UTF-8"` is always supported. Returns `(size_t) -1` on
error, with `errno` set (`E2BIG` when the output buffer is full).

name: Rf_StringFalse
summary: Test whether a C string represents false or true.
signature:
Rboolean Rf_StringFalse(const char *);
Rboolean Rf_StringTrue(const char *);
returns: `TRUE` when the string represents false (`Rf_StringFalse()`) or true (`Rf_StringTrue()`); unrecognised strings yield `FALSE` from both.
notes:
Recognises the strings `as.logical()` accepts (`"T"`, `"TRUE"`,
`"false"`, ...); anything else returns `FALSE` from both.

name: Rf_isSymbol
summary: Test whether an object is a symbol.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is a symbol (`SYMSXP`), otherwise `FALSE`.
