name: Rf_install
summary: Create the symbol for a name, returning the existing symbol if already present.
returns: The symbol (`SYMSXP`) with the given name, creating it if necessary.
notes:
Symbols are never garbage collected, so `SYMSXP`s don't need to be
protected. Cache frequently used symbols to avoid repeated lookups.
`Rf_installChar()` takes a CHARSXP; `Rf_installTrChar()` is the same
but first translates the string to the native encoding.

name: R_MissingArg
summary: Access the missing/empty symbol.
notes: Used as the second argument in a call like `f(x, )`.

name: R_dot_defined
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".defined".

name: R_dot_Method
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".Method".

name: R_dot_packageName
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".packageName".

name: R_dot_target
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".target".

name: R_BaseSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "base".

name: R_BraceSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "{".

name: R_Bracket2Symbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "[[".

name: R_BracketSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "[".

name: R_ClassSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "class".

name: R_DeviceSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".Device".

name: R_DimNamesSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "dimnames".

name: R_DimSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "dim".

name: R_DollarSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "$".

name: R_DotsSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "...".

name: R_DoubleColonSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "::".

name: R_DropSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "drop".

name: R_LastvalueSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".Last.value".

name: R_LevelsSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "levels".

name: R_ModeSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "mode".

name: R_NaRmSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "na.rm".

name: R_NameSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "name".

name: R_NamesSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "names".

name: R_NamespaceEnvSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".__NAMESPACE__.".

name: R_PackageSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "package".

name: R_PreviousSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "previous".

name: R_QuoteSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "quote".

name: R_RowNamesSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "row.names".

name: R_SeedsSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for ".Random.seed".

name: R_SortListSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "sort.list".

name: R_SourceSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "source".

name: R_SpecSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "spec".

name: R_TripleColonSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for `":::"`.

name: R_TspSymbol
summary: Access the predefined symbol for "tsp".

name: PRINTNAME
summary: Get the print name of a symbol.
returns: The print name of the symbol `x` as a `CHARSXP`.
notes:
Returns the name as a CHARSXP; use `CHAR(PRINTNAME(x))` for a
`const char*`. There is no API setter — symbols are interned, so
create the symbol you want with `Rf_install()` instead.

name: Rf_GetOption1
summary: Retrieve the value of an R option.
returns: The option's value, or `R_NilValue` if it is not set.
notes:
The older two-argument `Rf_GetOption()` was removed from the headers
in R 4.6.0.

name: Rf_GetOptionDigits
summary: Retrieve the digits or width option.
returns: The current value of the `digits` or `width` option, respectively.

name: R_compute_identical
summary: Test whether two objects are identical.
returns: `TRUE` if the objects are identical under the given flags, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
The third argument is a bitmask of flags for non-default options (set a
bit to get the FALSE behaviour): 1 = !NUM_EQ, 2 = !SINGLE_NA,
4 = !ATTR_AS_SET, 8 = !IGNORE_BYTECODE, 16 = !IGNORE_ENV,
32 = !IGNORE_SRCREF. R's `identical()` default corresponds to 16.

name: R_atof
summary: Convert a string to a double.
signature:
double R_atof(const char *str);
double R_strtod(const char *c, char **end);
returns: The parsed `double` value; `R_strtod()` also sets `*end` to the first unparsed character.
notes:
These two are guaranteed to use '.' as the decimal point,
and to accept "NA".

name: R_tmpnam
summary: Create a name for a temporary file.
returns: `R_tmpnam()` and `R_tmpnam2()` return a newly allocated temporary file name to free with `R_free_tmpnam()`.
notes:
The returned string is dynamically allocated; free it with
`R_free_tmpnam()` (not `free()`). A `NULL` prefix or extension is
replaced by `""`.

name: acopy_string
summary: Copy a string into R_alloc-allocated memory.
returns: A copy of `in` in transient `R_alloc()` memory.
notes:
The copy uses transient `R_alloc()` memory, so it is freed
automatically when your `.Call` entry point returns.

name: R_ExpandFileName
summary: Expand a path containing ~ to a full path.
returns: The path with any leading `~` expanded.
notes: Needed because most C APIs don't understand `~`.

name: Rf_xlength
summary: Get the length of a vector.
signature:
R_xlen_t Rf_xlength(SEXP x);
R_len_t Rf_length(SEXP x);
returns: The length of `x`: `Rf_xlength()` returns an `R_xlen_t`, `Rf_length()` an `R_len_t`.
notes:
`Rf_xlength()` uses `R_xlen_t` and supports long vectors (length up to
2^64 - 1); `Rf_length()` is limited to `int` (2^31 - 1).
Also works on pairlists, where it is O(n).

name: Rf_lengthgets
summary: Set the length of a vector by creating a new vector of extended length.
signature:
SEXP Rf_lengthgets(SEXP x, R_len_t n);
SEXP Rf_xlengthgets(SEXP x, R_xlen_t n);
returns: A newly allocated copy of `x` with length `n`, padded or truncated as needed.
notes: `Rf_xlengthgets()` is the `R_xlen_t`-based variant for long vectors.

name: LENGTH
summary: Get the length of a vector.
signature:
int LENGTH(SEXP x);
R_xlen_t XLENGTH(SEXP x);
returns: The length of `x`: `LENGTH()` returns an `int`, `XLENGTH()` an `R_xlen_t`.
notes:
Uppercase variants of `Rf_length()`/`Rf_xlength()`, implemented as
macros in base R for efficiency.

name: IS_LONG_VEC
summary: Test whether a vector is a long vector.
returns: Non-zero if `x` is a long vector (length over 2^31 - 1), zero otherwise.
notes: True when a vector's length exceeds the `int`-based limit of 2^31 - 1.

name: Rf_allocVector
summary: Create a new vector of the given type and length.
returns: A freshly allocated vector of `type` and length `n`; atomic contents are uninitialized.

args.n: number of elements; `R_xlen_t` supports long vectors on 64-bit platforms.

notes:
Atomic vector contents are uninitialised; `VECSXP`/`EXPRSXP` elements are
`R_NilValue` and `STRSXP` elements are `""`. Attributes are unset.

name: Rf_ScalarLogical
summary: Create a vector of length 1 from the corresponding C type.
returns: A length-1 vector of the corresponding type holding `x`; `Rf_ScalarLogical()` returns a cached singleton.
notes:
For strings, use [`Rf_ScalarString()`](#Rf_ScalarString) or
[`Rf_mkString()`](#Rf_mkString) instead. `Rf_ScalarLogical()` returns cached
singletons and never allocates; the other `Rf_Scalar*()` variants always
allocate.

name: Rf_coerceVector
summary: Coerce an existing vector to a different type.
returns: A freshly allocated copy of `x` coerced to `newtype`.
notes: Errors if it can't coerce between `TYPEOF(x)` and `newtype`.

name: Rf_mkNamed
summary: Create a named vector of the given type.
returns: A freshly allocated vector of `type` with one element per name and the names attribute set.

args.names: a null-terminated array of `const char*` names.

notes:
The vector's length matches the number of names supplied, and its names
attribute is set from them.

name: Rf_allocVector3
summary: Create a new vector using a custom allocator.
signature: SEXP Rf_allocVector3(SEXPTYPE type, R_xlen_t n, R_allocator_t *allocator);
returns: A freshly allocated vector of `type` and length `n`, with payload memory from `allocator`.
notes:
Like `Rf_allocVector()`, but memory for the data payload comes from
`allocator`; pass `NULL` for plain `Rf_allocVector()` behaviour. Rarely
needed in package code.

name: LOGICAL
summary: Get a pointer to the underlying C array of an atomic vector.
returns: A writable pointer to the underlying C array of `x`.

args.x: a vector of the corresponding type.

notes:
For long vectors, cache the returned pointer and reuse it rather than
calling the accessor on every iteration.

name: STRING_ELT
summary: Get or set a single element of a character vector.
signature:
SEXP STRING_ELT(SEXP x, R_xlen_t i);
void SET_STRING_ELT(SEXP x, R_xlen_t i, SEXP v);
returns: `STRING_ELT()` returns the `CHARSXP` element at index `i` (not a copy); `SET_STRING_ELT()` returns nothing.
notes:
`STRING_ELT()` returns a `CHARSXP`, not an ordinary `SEXP` value; strings
use a pair of accessor functions rather than a plain C array.

name: VECTOR_ELT
summary: Get or set a single element of a list.
signature:
SEXP VECTOR_ELT(SEXP x, R_xlen_t i);
SEXP SET_VECTOR_ELT(SEXP x, R_xlen_t i, SEXP v);
returns: `VECTOR_ELT()` returns the element at index `i` (not a copy); `SET_VECTOR_ELT()` returns `v`.
notes:
`VECTOR_ELT()` may return any `SEXPTYPE`; lists use a pair of accessor
functions rather than a plain C array.

name: Rf_asLogical
summary: Extract the first value of a vector as a C type, coercing as necessary.
returns: The first element of `x` coerced to the corresponding C type; may be an `NA` sentinel such as `NA_INTEGER` or `NA_REAL`.

name: NA_LOGICAL
summary: Represent missing logical and integer values.
notes:
`NA_LOGICAL` and `NA_INTEGER` are both `R_NaInt` (currently `INT_MIN`);
`NA_STRING` is `R_NaString`.

name: NA_REAL
summary: Represent a missing double value.
notes:
Represented as an `NaN` with a specific bit pattern, per the IEEE 754
floating-point standard.

name: R_NaN
summary: Represent NaN and positive or negative infinity as doubles.
notes:
Use these constants, together with `NA_REAL`, for cross-platform-safe
NaN, infinite, and missing values.

name: ISNA
summary: Check a double for missing, NaN, or non-finite values.
returns: Non-zero if `x` is `NA` (`ISNA()`), `NaN` or `NA` (`ISNAN()`), or finite (`R_FINITE()`); zero otherwise.
notes:
These are macros; `R_IsNA()`, `R_IsNaN()`, and `R_finite()` are the
equivalent functions. Check `!R_FINITE()` for non-finite values.

name: R_IsNA
summary: Check a double for missing, NaN, or non-finite values.
returns: Non-zero if the argument is `NA` (`R_IsNA()`), `NaN` or `NA` (`R_IsNaN()`), or finite (`R_finite()`); zero otherwise.
notes:
Function equivalents of the `ISNA()`, `ISNAN()`, and `R_FINITE()` macros.
`R_finite()` is false for `NA`, `NaN`, `Inf`, and `-Inf`.

name: Rf_isLogical
summary: Test if an SEXP is a logical vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is an `LGLSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
No function tests for `RAWSXP` or `VECSXP`; use `TYPEOF(x) == RAWSXP` or
`TYPEOF(x) == VECSXP` instead.

name: Rf_isInteger
summary: Test if an SEXP is an integer vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is an `INTSXP` (including factors), otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
Factors are also `INTSXP`s, so `Rf_isInteger()` accepts both plain
integer vectors and factors; combine with `Rf_isFactor()` to distinguish
them.

name: Rf_isReal
summary: Test if an SEXP is a double vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is a `REALSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_isComplex
summary: Test if an SEXP is a complex vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is a `CPLXSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_isString
summary: Test if an SEXP is a character vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is a `STRSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_isExpression
summary: Test if an SEXP is an expression vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is an `EXPRSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_isNewList
summary: Test if an SEXP is a list (`VECSXP`) or `NULL`.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is a `VECSXP` or `NILSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
Matches `NILSXP`/`VECSXP`, so the result diverges from `is.list()` on
`NULL`: `Rf_isNewList(R_NilValue)` is true while `is.list(NULL)` is
false. Consider writing your own wrapper around `TYPEOF(x)` instead.

name: Rf_isVectorAtomic
summary: Test if an SEXP is an atomic vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is an atomic vector (`LGLSXP`, `INTSXP`, `REALSXP`, `CPLXSXP`, `STRSXP`, or `RAWSXP`), otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
Matches `LGLSXP`/`INTSXP`/`REALSXP`/`CPLXSXP`/`STRSXP`/`RAWSXP`, so the
result diverges from `is.atomic()` on `NULL`:
`Rf_isVectorAtomic(R_NilValue)` is false while `is.atomic(NULL)` is
true. Consider writing your own wrapper around `TYPEOF(x)` instead.

name: Rf_isVectorList
summary: Test if an SEXP is a pairlist or expression vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is a `LISTSXP` or `EXPRSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Matches `LISTSXP`/`EXPRSXP`.

name: Rf_isVector
summary: Test if an SEXP is any kind of vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is any kind of vector, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: The union of `Rf_isVectorAtomic()` and `Rf_isVectorList()`.

name: Rf_isNumber
summary: Test if an SEXP is a numeric-like vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is `LGLSXP`, `REALSXP`, `CPLXSXP`, or a non-factor `INTSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Matches `LGLSXP`/`REALSXP`/`CPLXSXP` and non-factor `INTSXP`.

name: Rf_isNumeric
summary: Test if an SEXP is a numeric-like vector.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is `LGLSXP`, `REALSXP`, `CPLXSXP`, or a non-factor `INTSXP`, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes: Matches `LGLSXP`/`REALSXP`/`CPLXSXP` and non-factor `INTSXP`.

name: Rf_copyVector
summary: Copy from one vector to another, recycling as necessary.
notes:
Use `Rf_duplicate()` instead if you just want to duplicate a vector
without recycling.

name: Rf_stringSuffix
summary: Extract the tail of a STRSXP.
returns: A freshly allocated `STRSXP` with each element replaced by its suffix starting at `fromIndex`.

args.fromIndex: the index to start the suffix from.

name: IS_SCALAR
summary: Test if an object is a scalar (a vector of length 1) of the given type.
signature:
#define IS_SCALAR(x, type) (TYPEOF(x) == (type) && XLENGTH(x) == 1)
#define IS_SIMPLE_SCALAR(x, type) (IS_SCALAR(x, type) && ATTRIB(x) == R_NilValue)
notes:
`IS_SIMPLE_SCALAR()` additionally requires that the object has no
attributes.

name: Rf_isVectorizable
summary: Test if a list can be converted into a vector.
returns: `TRUE` if every element of `x` is a vector of length 0 or 1, otherwise `FALSE`.
notes:
True when every element of the list or pairlist is a vector of length 0
or 1.

name: R_qsort
summary: Sort a numeric array in place using quicksort.
notes:
The dummy index argument is renamed to `II` to avoid problems with
g++ on Solaris.

name: R_isort
summary: Sort an int, double, or complex array in place.

name: rsort_with_index
summary: Sort a double array in place, reordering an index array alongside.

name: Rf_revsort
summary: Sort a double array in reverse order, reordering an index array alongside.

name: Rf_iPsort
summary: Partially sort an int, double, or complex array around the k-th element.

name: R_orderVector
summary: Compute an ordering permutation into an index array.
signature:
void R_orderVector (int *indx, int n, SEXP arglist, Rboolean nalast, Rboolean decreasing);
void R_orderVector1(int *indx, int n, SEXP x,       Rboolean nalast, Rboolean decreasing);
notes:
C equivalent of `order(..., na.last, decreasing)`; build `arglist` with
`Rf_lang2()` or `Rf_lang3()`. `R_orderVector1()` is the single-vector
version, equivalent to `order(x, na.last, decreasing)`.

name: Rf_any_duplicated
summary: Find the position of the first duplicated element of a vector.
signature:
R_xlen_t Rf_any_duplicated(SEXP x, Rboolean from_last);
R_xlen_t Rf_any_duplicated3(SEXP x, SEXP incomp, Rboolean from_last);
returns: The one-based index of the first duplicated element, or 0 if there are no duplicates.

name: Rf_isUnsorted
summary: Test whether a vector may be unsorted.
returns: `TRUE` if `x` may be unsorted, otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_match
summary: Find the positions of first matches between two vectors.
signature:
SEXP Rf_match(SEXP itable, SEXP ix, int no_match);
SEXP Rf_matchE(SEXP itable, SEXP ix, int no_match, SEXP env);
returns: A freshly allocated `INTSXP` the length of `ix` giving one-based match positions in `itable`, or `no_match` where unmatched.
notes:
In `Rf_matchE()`, `env` is used to look up `as.character` when
translating `POSIXlt`; rarely needed directly.

name: Rf_duplicated
summary: Identify duplicated elements of a vector.
returns: A freshly allocated `LGLSXP` the same length as `x`, `TRUE` at duplicated positions.

args.from_last: if `TRUE`, search from the last element.

notes: Returns an `LGLSXP` the same length as `x`.

name: STRING_PTR_RO
summary: Get read-only access to the elements of a character or list vector.
signature:
const SEXP *STRING_PTR_RO(SEXP x);
const SEXP *VECTOR_PTR_RO(SEXP x);
returns: A read-only pointer to the `SEXP` element array of `x`.
notes:
The read-only analogues of `STRING_PTR()`/`VECTOR_PTR()`; use them
when you only read elements so ALTREP and future representations
aren't forced to materialize a writable array.

name: R_allocResizableVector
summary: Create a vector that can grow in place up to a maximum length.
returns: A freshly allocated resizable vector of `type`, initially length 0, able to grow to `maxlen`.

args.maxlen: maximum length the vector can grow to.

notes:
Allocates `maxlen` elements up front; the vector starts at length 0 and
can be resized in place with `R_resizeVector()`. Experimental: the
interface may change in future R releases.

name: R_duplicateAsResizable
summary: Duplicate a vector as a resizable vector.
returns: A freshly allocated resizable copy of `x` that can grow up to its current length.
notes:
The copy keeps its current length and can grow up to that length with
`R_resizeVector()`. Experimental: the interface may change in future R
releases.

name: R_resizeVector
summary: Resize a resizable vector in place.

args.newlen: new length, at most the vector's maximum length.

notes:
The API replacement for the non-API `SETLENGTH()`/`SET_TRUELENGTH()`
idiom. Experimental: the interface may change in future R releases.

name: R_isResizable
summary: Test if a vector is resizable.
returns: `true` if `x` is a resizable vector, otherwise `false`.

name: R_maxLength
summary: Get the maximum length a resizable vector can grow to.
returns: The maximum length `x` can grow to.

name: DATAPTR_RO
summary: Get an untyped pointer to a vector's data.
returns: An untyped pointer to the data payload of `x`; `DATAPTR()` is writable, `DATAPTR_RO()` read-only.

name: INTEGER_RO
summary: Get a read-only pointer to the underlying C array.
returns: A read-only pointer to the underlying C array of `x`.

args.x: a vector of the corresponding type.

notes:
Read-only variants of `INTEGER()` etc. Use them when you only read:
the `const` pointer catches accidental writes, and ALTREP vectors can
avoid materialising a writable copy.

name: INTEGER_ELT
summary: Get or set a single element of an atomic vector.
returns: The `*_ELT()` getters return the element at index `i` as the corresponding C type; the `SET_*_ELT()` setters return nothing.

args.x: a vector of the corresponding type.

name: Rf_isNull
summary: Test whether an object is NULL.
returns: `TRUE` if `s` is `NULL` (`NILSXP`), otherwise `FALSE`.

name: Rf_asBool
summary: Extract a checked single logical value as a C bool.
signature:
bool Rf_asBool(SEXP x);
Rboolean Rf_asRboolean(SEXP x);
returns: The single logical value of `x` as a C boolean; never `NA` because `NA` inputs raise an error.

args.x: a vector coercible to a single logical.

notes:
Like `Rf_asLogical()`, but errors if the coerced value is `NA` (or
the input is not a single value), so the result is always usable as
a C boolean.

name: R_isnancpp
summary: Test for NaN in a way that is safe from C++ compiler optimisations.
returns: Non-zero if the argument is `NaN`, zero otherwise.
notes:
Only needed from C++; it backs the `ISNAN()` macro there. In C, use
`ISNAN()` directly.
